Crumb Notes

Why my sourdough stopped rising

For three weeks every loaf came out flat and dense, even though the starter doubled on schedule and the dough felt the same in my hands as it always had.

The culprit turned out to be the flour. The mill had switched to a softer winter wheat, and the lower protein meant the gluten could not hold the gas the starter produced.

Adding ten percent bread flour and cutting the bulk ferment by an hour fixed it. The crumb opened up again on the very next bake, and the crust browned evenly.

8 comments

  1. Same thing happened to me last January. I never thought to check whether the mill had changed anything about the wheat they use.

  2. Did you change the hydration as well? Softer flour usually wants a little less water, or the dough spreads before it has a chance to rise.

  3. I keep a bag of high protein flour around for exactly this reason and blend it in whenever the regular flour starts behaving oddly.

  4. Thanks for writing this up. My loaves have been flat since the autumn and I was about to throw out a perfectly healthy starter.

  5. A shorter bulk ferment helped me too, but I also had to shape more tightly, otherwise the loaf slumped as soon as it left the basket.

  6. Is ten percent enough with a very weak flour? I tried that and still needed closer to twenty before the crumb opened up properly.

  7. Worth asking the mill for the protein figure. Mine publishes it for every batch, and it varies more than you would expect.

  8. Great detective work. I would have blamed the starter, the oven, the weather and the kitchen before I ever suspected the flour.
